text: Birkhoff's theorem states that the Schwarzschild metric is the unique spherically symmetric vacuum solution. According to the book, an important corollary is that:
choices: a pulsating spherical star emits strong monopole gravitational radiation
there is no monopole gravitational radiation
the exterior field depends on the star's detailed internal density profile
spherically symmetric collapse cannot produce a black hole
explanation: Because even a pulsating spherical star has a static Schwarzschild exterior, there is no monopole gravitational radiation — the book's stated corollary. This is the GR analog of Gauss's law / Newton's shell theorem: the exterior field depends only on the total mass M, not on the internal profile. Spherically symmetric collapse does in fact form a Schwarzschild black hole.
